script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: Shattered Mirrors

INT. NEW YORK APARTMENT - NIGHT

Our PROTAGONIST, ROBERT, sits at a small writing desk. He's in his late thirties, a man with a sharp jawline and deep-set eyes, which carry the weight of the world. He's been staring at a blank page for hours.

Robert: (to himself) I can do this. I have to do this. I've got talent. I've got the drive. I've got the ambition. (He smirks) But do I have the will?

The phone rings. Robert hesitates, then picks it up.

---

EXT. CITY STREET - DAY

Robert stands on a busy New York City street. He's talking on his cell phone.

ROBERT: (into phone) I'll meet you there. (He hangs up)

---

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Robert sits across from his mentor, MARGOT, an elderly woman with a warm smile. She's a successful author, and she's taken Robert under her wing.

Margot: So, Robert. You've been working on your novel for months now. How's it coming?

Robert: (sighs) It's a struggle. I keep getting distracted. I can't seem to focus.

Margot: (smiling) Writing is a process, Robert. It takes time and patience. But you have the talent. Don't give up on yourself.

---

INT. NEW YORK APARTMENT - NIGHT

Robert sits at his writing desk, staring at the blank page once more. He hears a knock on the door. It's his neighbor, EMMA, a young artist.

Emma: (cheerfully) Hey, Robert. I was just passing by and thought I'd check in on you. How's the writing going?

Robert: (sighs) The same as always.

Emma: (sympathetically) I know it can be frustrating, but don't give up. Keep going. You'll get there.

---

EXT. CENTRAL PARK - DAY

Robert and Emma sit on a bench in Central Park, feeding the pigeons. They talk about their dreams and aspirations.

Emma: I've always wanted to have a solo art exhibition. But I've been too afraid to put my work out there. What about you, Robert? What's holding you back?

Robert: (thoughtfully) Fear, I suppose. Fear of failure. Fear of rejection.

Emma: (nods) I understand that. But you have to remember, every successful person has faced rejection at some point in their lives. It's just a part of the process.

---

INT. NEW YORK APARTMENT - NIGHT

Robert sits at his writing desk, with a newfound determination. He begins to type, his fingers flying across the keyboard.

---

EXT. NEW YORK STREET - DAY

Robert walks down the busy New York City street, his mind focused on his writing. He passes by a bookstore and decides to stop in.

INT. BOOKSTORE - DAY

Robert browses the shelves, looking for inspiration. He comes across a book by Margot, his mentor. He picks it up and begins to read.

---

INT. NEW YORK APARTMENT - NIGHT

Robert sits at his writing desk, the words flowing freely from his mind to the page. He's in the zone, completely absorbed in his writing.

---

EXT. CENTRAL PARK - DAY

Robert sits on a bench in Central Park, reading over what he's written. He's pleased with his progress, but he knows there's still a long way to go.

---

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Robert meets with Margot once more. He shares his progress with her, and she's proud of him.

Margot: (smiling) I've always believed in you, Robert. And I can see now that you believe in yourself. Keep going.

---

INT. NEW YORK APARTMENT - NIGHT

Robert sits at his writing desk, the final pages of his novel in front of him. He's done it. He's finished his novel. He's achieved his ambition.

Robert: (to himself) I did it. I finished my novel.

---

EXT. NEW YORK STREET - DAY

Robert walks down the busy New York City street, a smile on his face. He's no longer weighed down by his fears and doubts. He's a successful writer, and nothing can stop him now.

FADE OUT.

---

END OF SCREENPLAY.
